sections.title: Carousel — every setting
sections.summary: An auto-advancing slide deck — the slide template, total play time, each slide’s text and picture and timing, and the per-slide text/image styles. This guide documents every setting of the Carousel block, grouped by area. Each setting matches a real control in the screen editor.

sections.title: Carousel section
sections.summary: Configures a Carousel screen — a set of slides (image plus optional text) that auto-advance on a timer to tell a quick visual story. Use it for a punchy intro, and keep slides few and fast so visitors reach the next step.

sections.title: Where it appears
sections.summary: Covered screen types: Carousel.

sections.title: Extra line look
sections.summary: Open this to override the third line's font size, weight, color, alignment, and the padding around it; it appears only with the Image + Title + 2 Subtitles template. Style it as the smallest, quietest text so it never competes with the headline or supporting line. Leave it on theme defaults unless you truly need a change, since overrides apply to this line on every slide of the carousel.

sections.title: Total play time
sections.summary: The total time in seconds for the whole carousel to play through once before it stops or the visitor moves on (0.1–120s). This total is split across slides by each slide's timing slider, so changing it speeds up or slows every slide proportionally. Start around 3–5 seconds per slide (about 12–20s for four slides) — long enough to read each line, short enough to keep momentum and avoid stalling the visitor.

sections.title: Image box height and position
sections.summary: Controls the box that holds each slide's image, separate from the image's own styling. Set how tall the box is (Auto fits the image, Fixed is an exact pixel height, Percent is a share of the slide), where the image sits inside it, and the padding around it. Leave it on Auto unless you want every slide's image to occupy the same vertical space so slides don't jump in size as visitors swipe.

sections.title: Image size and fit
sections.summary: Open this to control the slide image's width, height, corner radius, and how it fills its box: Fit shows the whole image (may leave bands), Fill covers the box (edges may crop), Crop trims to the exact box, and Tile repeats it. You also set the padding around the image. Fill is the usual choice for full-bleed slides and Fit keeps the whole graphic visible; settings apply to the image on every slide.

sections.title: Slide extra line
sections.summary: A third text line below the supporting line, available only with the Image + Title + 2 Subtitles template. Use it sparingly for one last small detail like a disclaimer or extra proof, since four text layers over an image quickly overcrowd a slide and slow reading. Supports @variable personalization, countdown timers, and styled chips, and is edited per language.

sections.title: How long this slide shows
sections.summary: A two-thumb slider that sets the window, as a share of the carousel's total duration, during which this slide is on screen. Drag the thumbs apart to give this slide a longer share, which leaves less time for the others. For example, a 25% window at a 20-second total keeps this slide visible about 5 seconds; keep slides spread evenly and only widen the most persuasive one.

sections.title: Slide picture
sections.summary: The image shown on this slide, required on every slide no matter which template you pick. Drag-and-drop or click to upload, and Segmently serves a fast-loading optimized version automatically. Use a high-quality picture that matches the slide's message; how it fills the slide is set in Image styles below, and a slide left without an image shows blank, so set one on every slide before publishing.

sections.title: Slide supporting line
sections.summary: The line under the headline, shown only when the slide template is Image + Title + Subtitle or richer. Use it to back up the headline with a quick proof point or detail rather than repeat it. It supports @variable personalization, countdown timers, and styled chips, is edited per language, and only appears after you set a slide template that includes a subtitle.

sections.title: Slide headline
sections.summary: The main headline on this slide, shown only when the slide template includes a title. Keep it short and benefit-led so it lands in the few seconds the slide is on screen. You can drop in the visitor's earlier answers with @variable, plus countdown timers and styled label chips; if your funnel runs in several languages, you edit this text per language.

sections.title: Slide content template
sections.summary: Sets which layers each slide shows: Image Only is just the picture, Image + Title adds one headline, Image + Title + Subtitle adds a supporting line, and Image + Title + 2 Subtitles shows all four text layers. Choosing a richer template reveals its matching text and style fields below. Default to Image + Title for clean, fast-reading slides and add subtitles only when each slide genuinely needs more copy.

sections.title: Supporting line look
sections.summary: Open this to override the supporting line's font size, weight, color, alignment, and the padding around it; it shows only when the template includes a subtitle. Keep this line visually lighter than the headline (smaller or thinner) so the slide reads in the right order. Leave it on theme defaults for consistency unless this carousel needs a custom look, and remember changes apply to every slide.

sections.title: Text box height and position
sections.summary: Controls the box that holds all of a slide's text (title, subtitle, detail) as a group, separate from styling each line. Set how tall the box is (Auto fits the text, Fixed is exact pixels, Percent is a share of the slide), where the text block sits, and the padding around it. Leave it on Auto unless you want text anchored the same way on every slide, for example always sitting in the lower third over the image.

sections.title: Title look and spacing
sections.summary: Open this to override how the carousel's headline looks: font size, weight, color, alignment, and the padding around the text. It only shows when the template includes a title. Leave it untouched to inherit your theme so screens stay consistent; change it only when one carousel needs a bigger or bolder headline, and note the overrides apply to the title on every slide.

Set how tall the box is (Auto fits the text, Fixed is exact pixels, Percent is a share of the slide), where the text block sits, and the padding around it. Leave it on Auto unless you want text anchored the same way on every slide, for example always sitting in the lower third over the image.

subarticles.title: Total play time
subarticles.summary: The total time in seconds for the whole carousel to play through once before it stops or the visitor moves on (0.1–120s). This total is split across slides by each slide's timing slider, so changing it speeds up or slows every slide proportionally. Start around 3–5 seconds per slide (about 12–20s for four slides) — long enough to read each line, short enough to keep momentum and avoid stalling the visitor.

translations.en: An auto-advancing slide deck — the slide template, total play time, each slide’s text and picture and timing, and the per-slide text/image styles. This guide documents every setting of the Carousel block, grouped by area. Each setting matches a real control in the screen editor.

en.name: The screen editor with the Carousel section highlighted.

translations.en: Open the Carousel section in the screen editor to configure its settings.

nodes.label: Slide template & content · Slide content template

translations.en: Sets which layers each slide shows: Image Only is just the picture, Image + Title adds one headline, Image + Title + Subtitle adds a supporting line, and Image + Title + 2 Subtitles shows all four text layers. Choosing a richer template reveals its matching text and style fields below. Default to Image + Title for clean, fast-reading slides and add subtitles only when each slide genuinely needs more copy.

en.name: Where to find “Slide content template” in the editor.

translations.en: The main headline on this slide, shown only when the slide template includes a title. Keep it short and benefit-led so it lands in the few seconds the slide is on screen. You can drop in the visitor's earlier answers with @variable, plus countdown timers and styled label chips; if your funnel runs in several languages, you edit this text per language.

en.name: Where to find “Slide headline” in the editor.

nodes.label: Slide template & content · Slide supporting line

translations.en: The line under the headline, shown only when the slide template is Image + Title + Subtitle or richer. Use it to back up the headline with a quick proof point or detail rather than repeat it. It supports @variable personalization, countdown timers, and styled chips, is edited per language, and only appears after you set a slide template that includes a subtitle.

en.name: Where to find “Slide supporting line” in the editor.

nodes.label: Slide template & content · Slide extra line

translations.en: A third text line below the supporting line, available only with the Image + Title + 2 Subtitles template. Use it sparingly for one last small detail like a disclaimer or extra proof, since four text layers over an image quickly overcrowd a slide and slow reading. Supports @variable personalization, countdown timers, and styled chips, and is edited per language.

en.name: Where to find “Slide extra line” in the editor.

translations.en: The image shown on this slide, required on every slide no matter which template you pick. Drag-and-drop or click to upload, and Segmently serves a fast-loading optimized version automatically. Use a high-quality picture that matches the slide's message; how it fills the slide is set in Image styles below, and a slide left without an image shows blank, so set one on every slide before publishing.

en.name: Where to find “Slide picture” in the editor.

translations.en: The total time in seconds for the whole carousel to play through once before it stops or the visitor moves on (0.1–120s). This total is split across slides by each slide's timing slider, so changing it speeds up or slows every slide proportionally. Start around 3–5 seconds per slide (about 12–20s for four slides) — long enough to read each line, short enough to keep momentum and avoid stalling the visitor.

en.name: Where to find “Total play time” in the editor.

nodes.label: Timing & duration · How long this slide shows

translations.en: A two-thumb slider that sets the window, as a share of the carousel's total duration, during which this slide is on screen. Drag the thumbs apart to give this slide a longer share, which leaves less time for the others. For example, a 25% window at a 20-second total keeps this slide visible about 5 seconds; keep slides spread evenly and only widen the most persuasive one.

translations.en: Open this to override the supporting line's font size, weight, color, alignment, and the padding around it; it shows only when the template includes a subtitle. Keep this line visually lighter than the headline (smaller or thinner) so the slide reads in the right order. Leave it on theme defaults for consistency unless this carousel needs a custom look, and remember changes apply to every slide.

Leave it on theme defaults unless you truly need a change, since overrides apply to this line on every slide of the carousel.

nodes.label: Slide text & image styles · Image size and fit

translations.en: Open this to control the slide image's width, height, corner radius, and how it fills its box: Fit shows the whole image (may leave bands), Fill covers the box (edges may crop), Crop trims to the exact box, and Tile repeats it. You also set the padding around the image. Fill is the usual choice for full-bleed slides and Fit keeps the whole graphic visible; settings apply to the image on every slide.

Leave it on Auto unless you want every slide's image to occupy the same vertical space so slides don't jump in size as visitors swipe.
